title: CausalOps Formal Causal Queries Specification
description: Mathematical formalization of 5 core causal inference queries required for root-cause analysis, counterfactual validation, and failure prevention in CausalOps.

queries.question: What downstream telemetry changes across the microservice topology are causally attributable to an intervention at candidate service X?
queries.mathematical_formulation: P(Y_{downstream}(t + delta) | do(X_s = x_fault), X_{pre}(t) = x_0)

outputs.affected_subgraph: Set of services {s' in Nodes | Delta Y_{s'} > tau_significance}
outputs.sla_impact: Predicted delta in api-gateway.p99_latency and api-gateway.error_rate

assumptions: Causal sufficiency over the 5-node microservice boundary
Stable structural equations governing inter-service RPC delays
Absence of unobserved exogenous network partitions during the intervention window
queries.identifiability_justification: Under controlled fault injection, the intervention do(X_s = x_fault) is directly implemented, truncating incoming edges into X_s. The truncated factorization formula (G-formula) permits direct identification from experimental or SCM post-intervention distributions.

evaluation_criteria.metric: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) against observed downstream degradation during active fault window
evaluation_criteria.ground_truth_reference: fault_parameters['latencyMs'] or fault_parameters['errorRate'] applied to attenuation laws

queries.query_name: Root-Cause Comparison (Explanatory Attribution / Posterior Root Cause)
queries.question: Given an observed incident degradation profile, which candidate service intervention best explains the observed multi-service symptoms?
queries.mathematical_formulation: arg max_{s in S_candidates} P(do(X_s = fault) | E_obs) = arg max_{s} [ P(E_obs | do(X_s = fault)) * P(s) ] / sum_k [ P(E_obs | do(X_k = fault)) * P(k) ]

inputs.observed_incident_telemetry: Multivariate time series E_obs in R^[T_incident, N, F]
inputs.prior_probabilities: P(s) (uniform 0.25 by default, or historical failure rate prior)

outputs.ranked_root_causes: Ranked list of candidate services with posterior explanatory likelihoods
outputs.confidence_score: Normalized posterior probability of top candidate

assumptions: Single-fault assumption per incident episode (verified by dataset generator: 1 fault injected at a time)
Incident is caused by one of the modeled microservice failure archetypes
No unobserved simultaneous external catastrophe causing independent failures in multiple tiers
queries.identifiability_justification: Because candidate interventions form a discrete mutually exclusive set S_candidates and downstream symptom vectors are distinct across branches (e.g. inventory DB faults do not affect payment, payment faults do not affect DB), the candidate likelihoods are distinct and identifiable.

evaluation_criteria.metric: Exact Match Top-1 Accuracy and Top-2 Recall

queries.question: If the candidate root cause had NOT degraded (i.e. had remained healthy), would the observed incident and downstream cascade have occurred?

pearl_three_step_procedure.step_1_abduction: Compute the specific exogenous noise terms u = {epsilon_i(t)} consistent with the factual observed telemetry E_obs: u_i(t) = X_i(t) - f_i(PA_i(t), X_i(t-1))
pearl_three_step_procedure.step_2_action: Modify the structural causal model by replacing the structural equation of node s with the healthy baseline condition: do(X_s(t) = X_{s, baseline}(t))
pearl_three_step_procedure.step_3_prediction: Propagate the abducted noise u through the modified structural equations to compute the counterfactual trajectory Y_{CF}(t) for all downstream nodes

outputs.counterfactual_telemetry: Simulated trajectory Y_{CF}(t) for all nodes if s were normal
outputs.remediation_efficacy_verdict: Boolean: True if Y_{api-gateway, CF} returns to healthy SLA threshold (< baseline * 2)

assumptions: Additive exogenous noise model: X_i = f_i(PA_i) + epsilon_i
No structural changes in physical network topology between factual and counterfactual worlds
queries.identifiability_justification: Under linear/additive SCMs with invertible noise, Pearl's abduction step uniquely identifies the exogenous background state u from factual observations. Action and prediction are deterministic forward evaluations in the mutilated graph.

evaluation_criteria.metric: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) against pre-fault baseline and post-clearance recovery telemetry
evaluation_criteria.ground_truth_reference: Pre-fault window [0, t_start) and post-fault recovery window [t_end, finished_at]

queries.question: Through which directed sequence of microservice variables does the failure propagate, and what is the temporal lag at each hop?

inputs.time_series_observations: Continuous telemetry matrix X in R^[T, N, F]

outputs.propagation_path: Ordered chain of active edges (e.g. inventory-db.db_latency -> inventory-service.p99_latency -> order-service.p99_latency -> api-gateway.p99_latency)
outputs.hop_delays: Estimated propagation lag per edge in seconds (e.g. lag=1s per inter-service hop)
outputs.path_attenuation: Cumulative product of transmission coefficients along the path

assumptions: Propagation occurs strictly along physical network call connections (respecting system-knowledge graph constraints)
Monotonic transmission: degradation upstream causes degradation downstream
Sampling interval (1.0s) is sufficient to observe or bound inter-service delay stages
queries.identifiability_justification: With topological constraints eliminating shortcut and cross-branch edges, the path between any candidate root and api-gateway is unique (or tree-structured). Lagged regression coefficients over discrete time steps uniquely determine path weights.

evaluation_criteria.metric: Pathway Path-Match Accuracy and Delay Lag Estimation Error (|tau_estimated - tau_actual|)
evaluation_criteria.ground_truth_reference: Known call graph path and step-inflection timestamps in telemetry

queries.query_name: Intervention Effect (Average Treatment Effect on Downstream Metrics)
queries.question: What is the expected quantitative shift in gateway SLA metrics under an active fault intervention versus normal baseline?
queries.mathematical_formulation: ATE(s -> gateway) = E[ Y_{gateway}(t) | do(X_s = x_fault) ] - E[ Y_{gateway}(t) | do(X_s = x_normal) ]

outputs.average_treatment_effect: Numerical delta in gateway latency (ms) and error rate (%)
outputs.severity_classification: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL based on SLA breach thresholds

assumptions: Consistency: Y(x) = Y whenever X = x
Positivity: P(X_s = x) > 0 for all evaluated intervention levels
Exchangeability: (Y(x_fault), Y(x_normal)) independent of X_s under randomized injection
queries.identifiability_justification: Because fault injections in CausalOps are randomized experimental trials, unconfoundedness holds by design for experimental data: P(Y | do(X = x)) = P(Y | X = x, injected). Identifiable via empirical sample means across matched experiments.

evaluation_criteria.ground_truth_reference: Difference between control experiment averages and fault experiment averages
